title: Quasi-coherence from the affine annihilator image
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $J$ quasi-coherent ideal sheaf data of finite type [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], and $F$ a quasi-coherent module sheaf [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $G$ be a module sheaf and $\iota:G\to F$ a monomorphism. Assume that for every affine open $U$, the image of $\iota(U)$ consists exactly of the sections $s$ killed by every $a\in J(U)$. Then $G$ is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Properties, Tag 01PO (lemma-sections-annihilated-by-ideal), proof; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PO

proof.text: On an affine open write F as M tilde and the ideal as I tilde. Finite type gives finitely many generators of I. Set M prime to the submodule killed by I. The assumed affine image formula identifies G(U) with M prime and identifies G(D(f)) with the annihilator of I_f in M_f.

source.place: Properties, Tag 01PO (lemma-sections-annihilated-by-ideal), proof; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PO

proof.text: Localization of the inclusion M prime into M is injective. For m/f^n killed by I_f, clear a power of f for each generator of I, then take the maximum exponent e. The numerator f^e m is in M prime and m/f^n is its fraction with denominator f^(n+e). For the empty generator family choose e=0. Thus the localized inclusion has precisely the required annihilator image.

source.place: Properties, Tag 01PO (lemma-sections-annihilated-by-ideal), proof; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PO

proof.text: The image identifications commute with restrictions because all inclusions into F do. They uniquely identify G with M prime tilde on the principal-open basis, and hence on the affine open. Every point has an affine neighborhood, so G is quasi-coherent.

theorem annihilator_subsheaf_quasicoherent (X : Scheme.{u}) (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    [J.toModules.IsFiniteType] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (G : X.Modules) (ι : G ⟶ F) [Mono ι]
    (himage : ∀ (U : X.affineOpens) (s : Γ(F, U.1)),
      s ∈ Set.range (ι.app U.1) ↔ ∀ a ∈ J.ideal U, a • s = 0) :
    G.IsQuasicoherent
